Definition: to advise; reflexively, to deliberate or resolve
BiblicalUsage: Jethro said to Moses, hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee. Balaam offered to advertise Balak what Israel would do, Ahithophel was David's counsellor, and Nathan gave Bathsheba counsel that she might save her own life and her son's.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that counsel is one of God's ordinary gifts and one of His great dangers: Jethro's counsel saved Moses from collapse, and Ahithophel's counsel nearly destroyed David, and the difference was whose cause the counsellor served. I believe the wise ask for counsel before they act, and the wiser still ask whose counsel it is.
